title: Draw a pair of cafe curtains shut along their rod until the two leading edges meet within 2 cm
instruction: Close the curtains: draw both panels along the rod until their inner edges meet in the middle.
context: Closing a pair of cafe curtains is everyday cloth handling in any kitchen. Here two tier panels hang from clip rings on a thin spring tension rod in a small window frame on the table, each pushed open to its own side. The robot slides each panel's leading clip ring along the rod toward the middle; the ring drags its panel, the gathered cloth opens out of its folds, and the two leading clips should end side by side. It is hard because the loose rings tilt and swing when pushed below the rod, the light panels bunch and sway, the hand has to work under the rod and just above the folded cloth, each panel is out of reach of the other arm so both arms must work, and the hands have to take turns in the middle. Doing nothing, drawing only one panel, knocking a ring off the rod or leaving a hand on the cloth scores 0.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (bases 610 apart): x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. 1) Window frame: two pine 1 x 3 boards (19 x 64 mm, 380 long) stand upright, their 64 mm sides along x, centred on x = 170, inner faces at y = +230 and -230; each is screwed to a 200 mm piece of pine 1 x 4 (19 x 89 mm) lying flat on its outer side (x 70 to 270) and clamped to the table with a small C-clamp. 2) Rod: Kenney KN630/1 Strafford spring tension rod, white steel, 7/16 in (11.1 mm) across, adjustable 18-28 in, sprung between the boards' inner faces, level, its axis at x = 170 and 362 above the table. 3) Curtains: Lino Rosa cafe tier pair, two panels of 24 x 12 in (610 wide, 305 long), linen-cotton-polyester blend, about 32 g each (estimate). 4) Rings: Kenney window curtain clip rings, black steel, 1 in (25.4 mm) inside, set of 14 (12 used), about 9 g each (estimate); clip about 12 wide, 6 thick and 16 tall (estimate). Six rings per panel clip its top hem every 122 mm: the first with its clip's side flush with the panel's inner edge, the last at the outer corner; the cloth's top hangs 48 below the rod's axis, so the hems clear the table by about 10 (estimates; ruler). 5) Start, open: the left panel's leading clip at y = +111 (its edge at +105), the next ring at +165, then +179, +193, +208 and +222; the right panel the mirror image; the cloth between each two clips in one fold, the first on the far side of the rod, then alternately near and far. Both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. Ring-on-rod friction about 0.2 (estimate; tilt the rod until a ring slides: friction = tan of that angle).
scoring: Judged at the end of the run from the top-camera video, a top photo and a ruler. Gap: the widest distance between the two panels' inner side edges, measured across at the clips, halfway down and at the hems (negative where they overlap). A panel is drawn when its leading clip ring has moved at least 5 cm toward the middle. Score 0 if either gripper still holds a curtain or its tool point (between the fingertips) is within 2 cm of one, the curtains are still moving (any point more than 1 cm from where it was 1 s earlier), a ring came off the rod at any time, or either panel is not drawn (doing nothing scores 0; the start gap is 21 cm). Otherwise the lowest of: (1) closure: 1.0 if the gap is at most 2 cm; 0.75 if over 2 and at most 5 cm; 0.5 if over 5 and at most 10 cm; 0.25 if over 10 cm. (2) rod: 1.0 if no cloth lies over the rod; 0.5 if some does.
reset_notes: About 1 minute. Open both grippers and send both arms to the ready pose. Check that every ring hangs on the rod and that the rod is level with its axis 362 mm up (ruler). Slide each panel back open: its leading clip's middle 111 mm from the middle of the rod (a pencil mark on the rod), the next ring at 165 mm, the other four about 14 mm apart up to the board. Settle the cloth by hand into one fold between each two clips, the first on the far side of the rod, then alternately near and far, and let the panels stop swinging. Re-clip any ring whose clip slipped on the hem (first clip flush with the panel's inner edge, the rest every 122 mm). Replace the curtain pair when it is creased hard, torn or stained; wash per its label.
fidelity: Each panel is PhysX cloth (1,922 nodes). Each ring is a rigid body that slides and swings on the rod by contact and friction; its clip holds its bite of cloth by a fixed attachment (no slip). Boards and rod are fixed. Panel mass 32 g, cloth stiffness and 2.5 mm thickness, ring mass 9 g, clip size and ring-on-rod friction 0.25/0.20 are estimates. Pads could hold cloth only by a contact-gated rule; the demo never grips.
